_comment: The period taxonomy, as data. Edit this file and re-run scripts/build_periods.py to
regenerate the period notes and the registry table together, so that note names,
en dashes, and the preceded-by/followed-by chain cannot drift apart by hand.
Changing this file is a schema change (§4) — it needs the user's approval, and every
event and claim already linking a renamed period must be migrated.

periods.name: Pre-Roman London
periods.label: before 43
periods.blurb: Thames-valley prehistory before the invasion of 43: Neolithic and Bronze Age activity along the river, Bronze Age timber structures and weapon deposits, and the Iron Age territories of the Trinovantes and Catuvellauni.
periods.note:
The starting bound of 4000 BCE is a convention, not a finding — it marks roughly where Thames-valley evidence becomes continuous rather than scattered. Earlier Palaeolithic and Mesolithic material belongs in this period too; date it with its own ISO year and ignore the nominal bound.

The substantive point most sources make about this period is a negative one: there is no evidence of a substantial settlement on the site the Romans chose, which makes Londinium a foundation rather than a continuation. Where an author argues otherwise, that is a claim note (§8), not a correction to this period.

periods.name: Roman London
periods.blurb: Londinium founded after the invasion of 43, walled by c. 200, and largely abandoned as an urban centre in the decades after the withdrawal of 410.

periods.name: Saxon London
periods.blurb: The walled city stands mostly empty while Lundenwic grows along the Strand; Alfred re-occupies the walls in 886 and the burh becomes London again.

periods.name: Norman London
periods.blurb: Conquest, the Tower, the White Tower, the first charters, and the Anarchy. Short but structurally decisive for the City's liberties.

periods.name: Medieval London
periods.blurb: Mayoralty, guilds and livery companies, the Black Death, the Peasants' Revolt, and the long argument between the City and the Crown.

periods.name: Tudor London
periods.blurb: Dissolution of the monasteries redraws the map of the city; population growth, the first suburbs, and the Royal Exchange.

periods.name: Stuart London
periods.blurb: Civil War, the Great Plague of 1665, the Great Fire of 1666 and the rebuilding, the Bank of England, and the beginnings of the West End.

periods.name: Georgian London
periods.blurb: The gates come down, the squares go up, the docks are built, and London becomes the largest city in the world.

periods.name: Victorian London
periods.blurb: Railways, sewers, the Underground, the Metropolitan Board of Works, and the slums that all of it was meant to answer.

periods.name: 20th-Century London
periods.blurb: The Blitz and the rebuilding, the LCC and the GLC, post-war immigration, the collapse and reinvention of the docks.
